## Summary

This change makes the pipeline's automated status notes (the messages it posts on cards and pull requests when something needs attention) carry a hidden, machine-readable tag alongside the text a person already reads — the idea being that other parts of the system can act on that tag instead of guessing from wording. It also adds an automated check meant to make sure every one of those notices always carries the tag, so this never quietly breaks in the future.

The wiring itself works, and the fourteen notices it touches are proven to read exactly as they did before, just with the new tag appended — I ran the full test suite (4,649 tests) and it is green.

The problem is with the safety net. I tested it directly: I took one of the fourteen notices this change wires up, removed its tag by hand, and re-ran the automated check that is supposed to catch exactly that. It reported no problem. The check only watches the pathway used for pull-request comments; it does not watch the pathway used for card comments — which is how the majority of these notices are actually posted. So if someone later edits one of these card notices and accidentally drops the tag, nothing will catch it, and the guard this PR is built around will not do the job it's described as doing. Shipping it as-is means the fleet gets a completeness guard that looks solid but has a hole exactly where most of the traffic goes.

## For the fixing agent

**Confirmed defect — `scripts/check_act_receipts.py` cannot see the majority of the receipt sites it is meant to guard.**

Reproduction (run against the PR branch):

```
python3 - <<'EOF'
import sys, os, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, "scripts")
import check_act_receipts as guard
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(td, ".github", "workflows"))
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(td, "scripts"))
    with open(os.path.join(td, "scripts", "thing.py"), "w") as fh:
        fh.write('''
import linear_ops

def announce(ident):
    linear_ops.cmd_comment(ident, "some raw comment with no trailer, added in a hurry")
''')
    print("sites found:", guard.sites(td))
EOF
```
→ `sites found: []`

And directly against the shipped tree: I reverted `scripts/reconcile.py`'s `flag_stranded()` (around line 1067) from
```python
linear_ops.cmd_comment(ident, pipeline_act.receipt(
    "card-stranded", f"🚨 {WATCHDOG_TAG}: {reason}"))
```
back to the pre-PR raw form
```python
linear_ops.cmd_comment(ident, f"🚨 {WATCHDOG_TAG}: {reason}")
```
and re-ran both CI guards this PR relies on:
- `python3 scripts/check_act_receipts.py` → exit 0, "0 problem(s)"
- `python3 scripts/pipeline_act.py check` → exit 0, "0 problem(s)"

Neither noticed the regression. `check_act_receipts.py list` (against the unmodified branch) shows only 20 sites, all of them `gh pr comment` / `gh issue comment` / `_post_pr_note` call forms in `.github/workflows/*.yml` and `scripts/*.py` (`scripts/check_act_receipts.py:493-546` `shell_sites`/`shell_act_flags`, `:601-636` `python_sites`). `python_sites()`'s poster detection (`_PY_POSTER_FUNCTIONS = ("_post_pr_note",)` and `_PY_POSTER_ARGV` matching `subprocess.run(["gh", "pr"/"issue", "comment", …])`, `scripts/check_act_receipts.py:374-375`) never matches a call to `linear_ops.cmd_comment(...)` — the function `scripts/linear_ops.py:cmd_comment` posts via `gql()` straight to the Linear GraphQL API (`scripts/linear_ops.py:132` `def gql`, `API = "https://api.linear.app/graphql"`), never through `gh` or `_post_pr_note`. So no AST match is possible for that call shape, regardless of whether its body is composed or raw.

This matters because 8 of the 10 `reconcile.py` sites this very PR converts — `card-stranded` (×2), `intake-overdue`, `blocker-reference-broken`, `pr-without-checks`, `work-never-landed` (×2), `reviewer-unavailable`, `verdict-left-behind` — all post through exactly this invisible path. The guard's own docstring states its purpose is "does every site that posts one use it?" (`scripts/check_act_receipts.py:308`) and that without it "this card is true on the day it merges and false the first time somebody adds a recovery in a hurry" (`scripts/check_act_receipts.py:305-306`) — but for the Linear-card-comment pathway, it is already false today, on the day it merges, because the guard cannot see that pathway at all, composed or not.

The PR body's opening claim — "a new CI guard fails the build on any receipt site that does not [compose through the writer]" — is not accurate for this majority pathway. The test suite reflects the same blind spot: `tests/test_check_act_receipts.py` only builds synthetic sites using `gh pr comment` / `subprocess.run` / `_post_pr_note` forms; nothing in it exercises (or would fail against) an unwrapped `linear_ops.cmd_comment(...)` call, so the gap shipped with full test coverage of the narrower, incomplete scope.

**Fix**: extend `python_sites()` in `scripts/check_act_receipts.py` to also recognize `linear_ops.cmd_comment(ident, body, ...)` calls as poster sites (mirroring how `_post_pr_note` and the `gh` argv forms are handled — treat the second positional arg as the body expression, matching `--act=` flags the same way `_SHELL_ACT_FLAG` does for shell), then add a test in `tests/test_check_act_receipts.py` proving an unwrapped `linear_ops.cmd_comment` call is found (the mirror of `TestAnUnwrappedSiteIsFound`), and re-run the `flag_stranded()` revert-and-check reproduction above to confirm it now goes red before resubmitting.

Everything else checked out: full test suite green (4,649 passed, 562 subtests), `pipeline_act.py check` and `check_act_receipts.py` both exit 0 on the shipped tree, TDD commit order is correct (test commit precedes the implementation commit, verified with `check_tdd_commits.py`), the byte-identical body claims are proven by fixture-driven tests that actually execute the real emitting functions, and I found no scope creep — all fourteen changed sites match the card's own list.

## Summary

This change is meant to guarantee that every automatic action our pipeline takes — a retry, a hold, an escalation to a human — leaves a plain, machine-readable trail, and it adds a build check whose whole job is to stop anyone from ever again adding a new automatic notice that skips that trail.

For the fourteen cases it explicitly converts, the work is solid: I independently re-ran the full test suite (4,659 tests) and reproduced the author's own regression check, and both hold up exactly as claimed.

The problem is the build check itself. Its job is to watch every place in the pipeline that posts a note and force each one to either carry the trail or be logged as a known gap. I tested this directly by adding a brand-new, unlabeled automatic notice to the code and running the check — it passed silently. I then found the same blind spot already live today: a real notice the pipeline posts when its review process is temporarily down is running right now with no trail and no record that it's missing one, and the new safety check cannot see it at all. The same hole exists in at least eight other places across the pipeline's automation, including the human hand-off note on a stalled merge.

So the safety net this card is meant to build has real, demonstrated holes — and they sit exactly where a future change is most likely to add a new automatic notice that then goes untracked, which is the precise failure this work was commissioned to prevent. I'd hold this until the check actually covers those pathways or the PR states plainly which ones it is choosing not to cover yet and why.

## For the fixing agent

**Root issue:** `scripts/check_act_receipts.py`'s corpus is under-inclusive. It only recognizes three call shapes:
- literal `gh pr comment` / `gh issue comment` text in `.github/workflows/*.yml` (`_SHELL_POSTERS`, line ~77)
- `_post_pr_note` / `linear_ops.cmd_comment` **Python calls** inside `scripts/*.py` (`_PY_POSTER_FUNCTIONS`, line ~92, scanned only via `python_sites()` which globs `scripts/*.py`)

It does **not** recognize a shell invocation of the `linear_ops.py comment` CLI (i.e. `python3 .../scripts/linear_ops.py comment "$CARD" "$BODY"`) from inside a workflow YAML file as a receipt site at all — even though this reaches the exact same `cmd_comment()` GraphQL write the PR spent most of its narrative arguing was "the pathway most receipts actually take." `shell_act_flags()` only validates the *name* of an `--act=` flag when one is present; it never asks whether a bare (no-flag) `linear_ops.py comment` call should have one or be declared unconverted.

**Proof (reproduced on the PR branch, `dd7050b`):**
1. Added a new-and-unlabeled workflow step `python3 .bureau-pipeline/scripts/linear_ops.py comment "$CARD" "🚑 a brand new recovery, in a hurry, no trailer at all"` to an isolated tree and ran `guard.sites()` / `guard.problems()` — result: `sites found: []`, zero problems. The exact "recovery added in a hurry" scenario the module's own docstring says it exists to catch is invisible to it for this call form.
2. `guard.sites()` on the real shipped tree returns 78 sites, none of them in `.github/workflows/medic.yml`, `agent-task.yml`, `plan.yml`, `merge-gate.yml`, `channel-watch.yml`, or `red-main-repair.yml` — despite all of those files invoking `linear_ops.py comment` from shell (confirmed via `grep -rn "linear_ops.py comment"`).
3. A concrete live example that is currently unaccounted for: **`.github/workflows/medic.yml:155`** — `python3 .bureau-pipeline/scripts/linear_ops.py comment "$CARD" "🔌 The code reviewer was temporarily unavailable..."`. This is act-shaped (the pipeline decided not to retry and is reporting a hold/backoff) but is neither composed through `pipeline_act.receipt()` nor declared in `config/pipeline-acts.json`'s `unconverted` block, and the guard cannot see it to demand either.
4. A second, distinct blind spot of the same kind: `scripts/gate_note.py:200-207` (`create_comment`) posts via `gh api --method POST repos/.../issues/{pr}/comments`, called from `scripts/merge_gate.py`'s "waiting for human merge" note (see `gate_note.py:122`). This is a third posting mechanism the corpus's `gh pr comment` / `gh issue comment` literal-text match does not recognize either.

**Why this matters against the card:** the PR body's own emission list explicitly counts "the fix loop's blocker and attempt notices" among the fourteen converted sites and frames the whole exercise as closing every gap a `gh`-only guard would miss — the corpus was *already* widened once during review specifically because a card-comment pathway was found unscanned (`TestACardCommentIsAReceiptSite` in `tests/test_check_act_receipts.py`). The same class of gap survives one layer further out: a card comment posted from **shell** rather than from **Python** source. The "0 problems" the guard reports is not evidence of completeness; it's evidence the guard cannot see these sites, which is materially different from what the PR body claims ("a new CI guard fails the build on any receipt site that does not [compose]").

**Suggested fix:** extend `shell_sites()` (or add a parallel scanner) to recognize `linear_ops.py comment` (and ideally `gh api --method POST .../comments`) invocations in `.github/workflows/*.yml` as receipt sites, subject to the same compose-or-declare rule already applied to the other four forms. Every genuinely non-act posting this turns up (plan.yml's epic commentary, the merge-gate's human-wait note, etc.) can go in `unconverted` with a reason exactly as the other 63 entries do — the mechanism for handling them already exists, it's just not being asked to look at these files.

**Tests:** the new test suites (`test_act_emission.py`, `test_act_emission_scenario.py`, `test_check_act_receipts.py`) are real — I ran all 128 of them, and independently mutated a converted call site to confirm the guard actually goes red (matching the PR's own claimed reproduction). They are not vacuous; they simply don't cover the corpus gap above because the underlying scanner doesn't either.

**Everything else** (TDD commit order, CI status, JSON/YAML validity, vendor-boundary premortem, scope) checked out clean — this is the only blocking issue found.

## Summary
This change makes the automated pipeline explain itself when Linear's ticket system temporarily runs out of request quota, instead of failing with a cryptic, unexplainable error and forcing someone to manually re-run the failed request just to find out why. It also teaches the health-monitoring system to recognize "we're temporarily out of quota" as a self-resolving condition rather than treating it as a bug that needs investigation.

It delivers most of what the card asked for, and the team's own proof-of-work is thorough and convincing. But there is one gap that undercuts the core promise of the change: one of the two ways Linear can signal "you're out of quota" produces a message that the health-monitoring system fails to recognize. In that situation, the system would still investigate a false alarm and consume more of the very quota that is already exhausted — the exact problem this change exists to prevent. It only affects one of the two paths, so it will not misfire on every quota event, but it will misfire on the path the team explicitly built and claimed to have covered, and nothing in the test suite catches it.

## For the fixing agent

**Defect — `scripts/linear_ops.py:227-236`.** The 200-status-with-`errors`-payload branch of `gql()` raises:

```python
raise LinearRateLimited(
    f"linear error: {condition} — {errors[:BODY_CHARS]}"
)
```

This message never includes the `API` endpoint constant. `medic_classify.is_linear_rate_limited()` (`scripts/medic_classify.py`, new `_LINEAR_API_HOST` check) requires the host string `api.linear.app` and a rate-limit fingerprint to co-occur on the **same line** — a deliberate design choice to avoid classifying prose that merely quotes the payload (see the module docstring and `test_quoted_ratelimited_body_in_a_card_is_not_a_rate_limit`). Because this branch's message omits the host entirely, `is_linear_rate_limited()` returns `False` and `classify()` returns `"normal"` instead of `"linear_ratelimited"` for this exact exception.

Reproduced directly against the PR's code (ran locally, not simulated):

```
RAISED MESSAGE: 'linear error: rate limited: 2500 requests/hour exhausted — [{"message": "Rate limit
exceeded. Only 2500 requests are allowed per 1 hour and you have made 2500 requests in the last
hour.", "extensions": {"type": "ratelimited", "code": "RATELIMITED", "statusCode": 429, "userError": true}}]'
medic_classify.is_linear_rate_limited -> False
medic_classify.classify -> normal
```

This is exactly the codepath the PR body calls out ("Linear can also answer 200 with an errors payload. Same condition, same type") and claims covers acceptance criterion 3 ("A rate-limited sweep fails distinguishably and is not reported as a defect"). It does not: any script that hits this branch — including the guarded per-card `except linear_ops.LinearError` sites in `reconcile.py` (e.g. lines 1274, 1285, 1824, 2011, 2228, 2257, 4486, all pre-existing) that log the exception's `str(e)` — will produce a log line the medic misclassifies as `normal`, triggering the exact retry-then-diagnose-into-an-exhausted-quota loop (DRE-1921) this PR exists to stop.

**Fix:** include the `API` constant in this branch's message, matching `_api_error`'s shape, e.g.:
```python
raise LinearRateLimited(
    f"linear error from {API}: {condition} — {errors[:BODY_CHARS]}"
)
```

**Test gap that let this ship:** `tests/test_linear_error_body.py::test_ratelimited_in_a_200_errors_payload_is_also_named` only asserts the raised type is `LinearRateLimited` and that the condition string is in the message — it never asserts the message is still classifiable by `medic_classify.is_linear_rate_limited()`. Every other positive case in `tests/test_medic_linear_rate_limit.py` (e.g. `test_the_anchor_is_the_message_the_client_actually_composes`) exercises the real client message through the real classifier specifically to prevent the two halves drifting apart — this one code path is the one place that discipline was skipped, and it's exactly where the drift happened. Add an assertion (or a new test in `tests/test_medic_linear_rate_limit.py`) that feeds this branch's composed message through `medic_classify.is_linear_rate_limited()` and asserts `True`.

Everything else checked out:
- TDD commit order verified locally (`check_tdd_commits.py origin/main HEAD`): RED test commit `40dbdf9` precedes the implementation commit `d14200f`.
- All 28 new tests pass locally; CI's "scripts unit tests" and "TDD commit discipline" are both green (they don't catch this because, as above, nothing exercises this specific branch through the classifier).
- Sibling-audit claim verified by reading the other three `urlopen` sites directly: `dispatch_pool.py:_read_remaining_real` swallows via bare `except Exception: return None` (compliant under the audit's swallow rule), `model_fallback.py:_probe_real` has an explicit `except urllib.error.HTTPError` that reads the body, and `harness/github_api.py:_urlopen` is the documented module-scope fallback whose caller (`_attempt`, line ~122-123) reads the body. All three match the PR's stated disposition table.
- Vendor-boundaries checklist (Q1-Q5): PR body answers all five; medic.yml wiring is additive only (no new trigger, no new actor gate, no secrets), consistent with the existing `upstream_5xx` job shape.
- No scope creep — `model_catalog.py`'s fix is the explicitly-scoped sibling-audit item (AC5), not a drive-by.
- Not a repair-branch PR; no `**Design:**` ref, so visual QA correctly skipped.

Not blocking, but worth a look while in this file: the negative test (`test_quoted_ratelimited_body_in_a_card_is_not_a_rate_limit`) covers prose that quotes the raw JSON payload, but doesn't cover prose that quotes the *composed* message (host + condition on one line) — which is exactly the shape appearing in this PR's own body's proof block. Low risk today, but worth a fixture if card/PR text bearing that exact composed-message shape is ever echoed into a build log.

Every time we merge finished work, the system used to sweep the entire board twice — once to check if anything could move forward, once to check if any project had wrapped up — no matter whether that particular merge actually changed anything.
